messages:
lee: heads-up - onboarding morpheus13b int4 on A10G fleet. early canary shows sporadic OOMs when multiple long-turn requests overlap (~1.5k-2k gen). attaching short repro.

sasha: can you share runner args and runtime/kernel? suspect prefetch + large max_new_tokens + low kv_reserve.

lee: runtime v2.3.1, kernel=optimized-attn, args:
```
--quant int4 --prefetch=true --batch-size=12 --max_new_tokens=2048 --kv_reserve=0.12
```
logs:
```
[2026-03-22T11:02:01Z] slab stripe grow 64->192MB
[2026-03-22T11:02:02Z] kv_prefetch miss burst 75%
[2026-03-22T11:02:02Z] alloc fail 48MB -> GPU OOM
```

rafi: reproducible? run 3 concurrent 1500-token calls to see overlap. also which canary traffic percent?

lee: repro script posted: https://internal/ci/repro/morpheus-warmstart.sh. canary at 3% traffic. repro locally in a loop.

sasha: quick mitigations: lower max_new_tokens to 1024 for canary, reduce batch_size to 8, raise kv_reserve to 0.22, enable async_compact flag. These reduce memory pressure but may hurt latency.

jamie: tried local patch: max_new_tokens=1024, batch=8, kv_reserve=0.22, runtime.flag enable_async_compact=true. 2k runs, 0 OOMs, p95 latency +7%.

rafi: add CI smoke that runs 20 long traces and asserts NO_OOM and p95<=baseline*1.15. ci-bot?

ci-bot: created morpheus-int4-longtrace-smoke. threshold: 0 OOMs, p95<=baseline*1.15.

sasha: parallel concern: nightly quality eval shows small accuracy dip on long-list/structured outputs. schedule targeted A/B against int8 on the failing subset.

lee: agree. plan: ship defaults change to canary only (route<=5%), run quant-recal overnight, run batch12 and kernel-variant tests, and monitor slab histograms + kv miss heatmaps. If quality regressed >3% on eval, fallback route long-trace requests to int8.

jamie: filing rollout PR pinned to canary and adding smoke job gating. will monitor for 2h before expanding.

lee: rolling now. will report telemetry: initial KV miss down ~28%, slab growth stabilized, no OOMs in first 30m, p95 +8%. closing thread pending CI pass. thanks all.
